questions.prompt: Who salutes first when an Airman and an officer pass each other outdoors in uniform?
questions.explanation: The junior member salutes first and holds the salute until the senior returns it or passes.

questions.prompt: In general, when is a salute NOT required?
choices: When passing a senior officer on the sidewalk
When the National Anthem plays outdoors
questions.explanation: Salutes generally aren't exchanged indoors. The main exception is formally reporting to a senior officer.

questions.prompt: What is the standard way to formally report to an officer?
questions.explanation: Approach, halt, salute, and say "Sir (or Ma'am), Cadet [Last Name] reports as ordered." Hold the salute until it's returned.

questions.prompt: When walking with a senior officer, where should the junior member walk?
questions.explanation: The junior walks on the senior's left. The position of honor is on the right.

questions.prompt: When getting into a car with a senior officer, who gets in first?
questions.explanation: Juniors get in first and the senior gets in last. When getting out, the senior goes first.

questions.prompt: When the National Anthem plays outdoors and you are in uniform, you should:
choices: Face the flag or music, stand at attention, and salute
Place your hand over your heart
questions.explanation: In uniform outdoors, face the flag (or the music if you can't see it), come to attention, and salute from the first note to the last.

questions.prompt: Indoors, headgear (your hat) should normally be:
choices: Tucked under the arm only in formation
questions.explanation: Headgear is normally removed indoors. Exceptions include when you're under arms (carrying a weapon) on duty.

questions.prompt: What time is 1530 in military time?
questions.explanation: Subtract 1200 for afternoon times: 1530 minus 1200 is 3:30 PM.

questions.prompt: How is 9:45 PM written in military time?
questions.explanation: Add 1200 to PM times: 9:45 plus 12 hours is 2145.

questions.prompt: In the phonetic alphabet, what word stands for the letter "Q"?
questions.explanation: Q is Quebec. Nearby letters: O Oscar, P Papa, R Romeo, S Sierra.

questions.prompt: In the phonetic alphabet, what word stands for the letter "J"?
questions.explanation: J is Juliett, officially spelled with two T's. Nearby: I India, K Kilo, L Lima.

questions.prompt: Which word is "W" in the phonetic alphabet?
questions.explanation: W is Whiskey. Then X X-ray, Y Yankee, Z Zulu.

questions.prompt: Which word is "V" in the phonetic alphabet?
questions.explanation: V is Victor. Before it: T Tango, U Uniform.
Zulu time is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), so units in different time zones can share one clock.

questions.prompt: What should you do when the senior officer present enters a room where you are seated?
choices: The first person to see them calls the room to attention, and everyone stands
questions.explanation: Whoever notices first calls "Room, attention!" and everyone stands at attention until told otherwise. Detachments may have specific procedures, so follow local guidance.

questions.prompt: When you're in uniform and hear "Retreat" or "To the Colors" outdoors at the end of the duty day, the flag is being:
questions.explanation: Retreat marks the end of the duty day, when the flag is lowered. Reveille marks the start of the day, when it's raised.
